1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the token against the session's stored digest.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is tied to a specific session and token digest.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated upon password reset (session.passwordUpdated is set, and old sessions are not reused).

4.why: The website enforces HTTPS with HSTS and uses the latest TLS version (as evidenced by the TLS certificate requirement).

5.why: Reset codes are hashed with SHA-256, and user data is not stored in plaintext (passwords are hashed with bcrypt).

6.why: Email messages (simulated) do not expose private user data; test tokens are only shown in logs for demonstration.

7.why: User-supplied data (e.g., account, token, password) is validated and sanitized (e.g., regex checks, length limits).

8.why: Redirect links are safe and only point to the hospital’s site (e.g., recovery link uses location.pathname).

9.why: Email templates (simulated) contain no scripts or HTML from user input; all dynamic content is text-only.

10.why: Private information or tokens are not shown in error pages or logs (generic error messages are used).

11.why: Passwords and secret codes are stored securely (bcrypt for passwords, no hardcoded secrets in the code).

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; sessions and tokens are randomly generated.

13.why: The system bars users from making too many wrong attempts (throttling with THROTTLE_WINDOW and attempt counters).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic response for all recovery requests).

15.why: The password reset code is random (32-byte token), complex (hex-encoded), and user-specific (tied to session).
